evidence.excerpt: We compare user-based k-nearest-neighbour collaborative filtering, item-based kNN, and singular value decomposition-based matrix factorisation on a proprietary dataset provided by a mid-size Novi Sad online retailer, comprising 91,000 users and 6,400 products over 18 months of purchase history. Similarity metrics tested include cosine, adjusted cosine, and Pearson correlation. SVD with rank-40 decomposition achieves Precision@5 of 0.187 and Recall@5 of 0.143, outperforming item-based kNN (0.161 / 0.129) and user-based kNN (0.148 / 0.118) at the same cut-off. We document practical challenges specific to the dataset: extreme popularity skew, infrequent rebuying behaviour, and seasonal drift. The paper provides a replication guide so that practitioners with similarly sized datasets can reproduce the evaluation pipeline using open-source tools. All experiments run on commodity hardware within two hours.
